prayerExcerpt.en-US: Make us docile in believing the faith and courageous in confessing it.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Fazei-nos dóceis para acolher a fé e fortes para proclamá-la.

meta.face: Sixtus: a man of about sixty-five with a LONG, LEAN, NARROW face — a high, completely bald dome with only thin wisps of white at the temples, a long, strongly hooked nose, heavy-lidded pale blue eyes under thin white brows, flat cheeks, a long upper lip and a thin mouth; CLEAN-SHAVEN but for close white stubble on the jaw (no beard, no curls), the head slightly bowed and the gaze lowered gently toward the viewer as he teaches. Agapitus: a man of about thirty with a wide, flat-planed, rectangular face and a broad, square chin with a small cleft — a short, straight nose, wide-set level dark eyes under heavy straight black brows, a full mouth; close-cropped straight black hair, clean-shaven with a dark shadow on the jaw, looking toward the pope.
meta.basis: No early portrait of Sixtus survives; the card follows Raphael's Sistine Madonna (a bald, hook-nosed pope with a short curly grey beard looking upward); the card keeps his bald dome and hooked nose but drops the beard and the upward gaze, which would repeat the Cornelius card. Agapitus is one of the deacons martyred with him in the Liber Pontificalis; his face is our choice, kept apart from the Lawrence card.
